newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The South African rand was moving gradually deeper into positive territory as importer demand for dollars dried up in torpid late Tuesday dealings.
"It's been very quiet with very narrow spreads," commented one rand trader.
The rand was last at 4.4640/4670 from its late Monday level of 4.4680/4710.
Dealers said importer demand for dollars over the morning took the unit off its intraday best of 4.4585 but the afternoon resistance at 4.4660 encouraged exporters to take charge.
Dealers said there was little in the day's ahead to give the market clear direction but an upside bias was likely in the absence of large importer shocks.
"It's still going to be very rangebound for the rest of this week and early next week unless there are any big orders pending," said one dealer.
Dealers's market outlook for Wednesday marked out a likely range of 4.4575-4.4700 for the rand.
In cross rate dealings, the rand did little more than be jostled around by the U.S. dollar's fortunes.
"Most of the movements are nothing related to traded rates. The USD has had a hell of a day against the mark and particularly the yen," said one trader.
The rand was last at 0.3792/3797 marks from 0.3815/3818 late Monday and at 25.4169/4452 agains the yen from 25.9852/0251 before.
It was at 7.3414/3508 rand to the British pound from 7.3199/3293 rand previously.

In the bond market, yields drifted gently higher over the session as players kept their hands thrust deep in t(eir pockets while waiting for news from the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting, currently underway.
The R150 long bond was last at at 14.865 percent from 14.835 percent at Monday's close.
Despite having ears trained Stateside, dealers said the market would only feel short-term impact from a move in U.S. interest rates, the expectations for which remain divided.
"It doesn't change much here. Our (interest rate) cycles are still mismatched," said one bond trader.
Foreigners were net sellers of 596.73 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Monday after buying 88.09 million rand's worth on Friday, the Bond Exchange said.
The Reserve Bank said South Africa's money market shortage narrowed to 6.556 billion rand on Monday from 7.974 billion rand on Saturday.

A South African Reserve Bank money market spoieman said the narrower shortage reflected increased liquidity due to Monday's payments to the provinces from the Bank's Exchequer account instead of the Tax and Loan account, its usual source for these regular payments.

Domestic short term money market rates were were barely changed from Monday with three month NCD rates from major banks between 16.35 percent and 16.40 percent offered from 16.40 across the board on Monday, while 90-day BA rates remained at 15.90 percent.
One trader said there was some market concern about the offshore sales but he said most players would wait and see if it was the start of a long-term trend before becoming overly worried.
Nominal Bond Exchange turnover rose to 6.24 billion rand Monday from 5.27 billion rand on Friday.
-- Justin McCamish, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482-1003
